newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian groups form new anti-government alliance.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian groups form new anti-government alliance.

text.p: Thirty-three Nigerian human rights and pro-democracy groups have formed an alliance to campaign for an end to military rule, the leader of one group said on Tuesday.
"The broad aim is to terminate military rule as soon as possible," Ayo Obe, president of Civil Liberties Organisation, the leading human rights group in the country, told Reuters.

Called the United Action for Democracy (UAD), the new alliance would also try to scuttle any attempt by military ruler General Sani Abacha to become a civilian leader through next year's presidential election.
"We agreed to resist any tendency by the present head of state to succeed himself," Obe said.
"The UAD is to try to be a platform for all the groups to work towards our common objective which is enthronement of real democracy," she added.

Representatives of the 33 groups met in Lagos at the weekend and adopted a nine-point programme including a demand for the release of all political detainees, among them Moshood Abiola, the presumed winner of a 1993 annulled presidential vote.
Abiola has been detained since 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of Abacha, who seized power in the turmoil that followed the election annulment.
Abacha has promised to hand over to a democratically-elected president next year but his opponents say he plans to succeed himself.

Africa's most populous nation has been ruled by the military for most of its post independent period. It became a pariah when Abacha's government defied world opinion and hanged nine minority rights activists in 1995 for murder.
